title: GCL 2026, Day 6: One game point separates Alpine APL Pipers, FYERS American Gambits and Ganges Grandmasters at the top
summary: Alpine APL Pipers beat PBG Alaskan Knights 11-6 but lost to Ganges Grandmasters 4-12; CheQ Mumba Masters also stay in the hunt with a 14-5 win over Triveni Continental Kings; American Gambits beat the Grandmasters 13-5. The group stage of the fourth season of the Global Chess League (GCL), a joint initiative of Tech Mahindra and FIDE in Bengaluru, is heading to a nail-biting finale. With only two days left to play at the preliminary stage, just one game point separates the top three teams. Defending champions Alpine APL Pipers, FYERS American Gambits, and Ganges Grandmasters now have 15 Match Points each after eight rounds. The first two are slightly ahead with 73 Game Points, while the Grandmasters sit on 72. The Pipers and the Grandmasters had a chance to take the sole lead on Thursday, as they were scheduled to play two matches each. Ganges Grandmasters began the day with a convincing 12-4 win over the Alpine APL Pipers while playing with the Black pieces, but went down 13-5 in their final match of the day against the American Gambits. The Pipers went on to beat the PBG Alaskan Knights 11-6, and the CheQ Mumba Masters kept their chances of making it to the final alive with a 14-5 win over the Triveni Continental Kings. They now have 12 Match Points and 73 Game Points to show for their efforts. Let’s take a closer look at today’s matches: Alpine APL Pipers vs. Ganges Grandmasters: 4-12 The day began with the Ganges Grandmasters beating the Pipers without dropping a single game. Stavroula Tsolakidou started the Grandmasters’ march by inflicting a second loss of the tournament on Humpy Koneru. On the Superstar Men’s board, two-time World Cup winner Levon Aronian turned the tables on Anish Giri to win in 61 moves. “I got lucky, very lucky. But I always believed that I could find the best moves despite playing very badly at the start. Maybe not losing the game was what I deserved, but winning, of course, is a huge stroke of luck,” said Aronian, who was also named Player of the Match. With all other games drawn, the Ganges Grandmasters comfortably sealed the match. Triveni Continental Kings vs. CheQ Mumba Masters: 5-14In the day’s second match, the CheQ Mumba Masters kept their hopes of reaching the final alive with a thumping win over the Triveni Continental Kings. Playing with the Black pieces, the Mumba Masters won three out of six games, with Alexandra Kosteniuk scoring the only victory for the Continental Kings. On the Icon board, Maxime Vachier-Lagrave outplayed Alireza Firouzja, and Shakhriyar Mamedyarov defeated Aravindh Chithambaram on the Superstar Men’s board. With Bardiya Daneshvar also winning on the Prodigy board, the Mumba Masters took their Game Points tally to 73 from eight matches, securing their fourth win. Alpine APL Pipers vs. PBG Alaskan Knights: 11-6Magnus Carlsen set the tone in the match, prevailing over Viswanathan Anand in a complicated battle on the Icon board, while Humpy Koneru took revenge for her earlier loss to Nino Batsiashvili, extending the Pipers’ lead. Volodar Murzin then defeated Abhimanyu Mishra on the Prodigy board in a time scramble to put the result beyond doubt. Only 15-year-old Yagiz Kaan Erdogmus managed to score four points for a win with Black for the Alaskan Knights, as Vidit Gujrathi ran out of time on the Superstar Men’s board. FYERS American Gambits vs. Ganges Grandmasters: 13-5Aronian made it a double when he defeated Nihal Sarin of FYERS American Gambits in the last match of the day, but his team suffered a crushing 13-5 defeat. On the Icon board, Candidates 2026 winner Javokhir Sindarov won over Ian Nepomniachtchi, Daniil Dubov outplayed Leinier Dominguez Perez, Bibisara Assaubayeva handed Polina Shuvalova her first loss of the competition, and Marc’Andria Maurizzi claimed another three points after Luke Leon Mendonca ran out of time on the Prodigy board. Standings after Day 6 Schedule for Friday, September 11: 5.00 PM: Triveni Continental Kings vs PBG Alaskan Knights6.30 PM: Alpine APL Pipers vs FYERS American Gambits8.00 PM: Ganges Grandmasters vs CheQ Mumba Masters About the Global Chess League The Global Chess League (GCL), a joint initiative between Tech Mahindra and FIDE, is the world’s first and largest official franchise league of its kind. The league brings together leading chess players from across the globe in a unique joint team format, with six players representing each franchise across Icons, Superstar Men, Superstar Women and Prodigies. Men and women compete together on the same team, with every board carrying equal value towards the team’s result. GCL has previously staged seasons in Dubai, London, and Mumbai and returns to India for Season 4 in Bengaluru. GCL official website: https://globalchessleague.com/

title: 3rd FIDE Chess Olympiad for People with Disabilities opens in Samarkand
summary: Samarkand, Uzbekistan – September 10, 2026 Chess has a unique ability to dissolve boundaries, bringing people together across countries, cultures and different life circumstances. That spirit was at the heart of the opening of the 3rd FIDE Chess Olympiad for People with Disabilities, which welcomed a record 41 teams to Samarkand. The third edition marks an important milestone in the history of the competition. For the first time, the FIDE Chess Olympiad for People with Disabilities is being held alongside the main FIDE Chess Olympiad, bringing the two events together in the same host city and during the same period. The Olympiad for People with Disabilities gets underway first, with Round 1 on September 11, while the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad begins its competitive programme five days later, with Round 1 on September 16. The opening ceremony took place at the Hilton Hotel in Samarkand, bringing together players, officials and guests ahead of seven days of competition. “Power, passion and will” Welcoming the participants, Adkham Ikramov, Minister of Sports of the Republic of Uzbekistan, emphasized Uzbekistan’s commitment to chess and thanked FIDE for the trust placed in the country to host such an important event. He highlighted the support of the President of the Republic of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, as well as the work of the government, the Chess Federation of Uzbekistan and the Samarkand authorities in preparing the competition. Speaking both as Minister of Sports and as a medical doctor, Ikramov said that it was especially meaningful for him that this major gathering of the chess world begins with the Olympiad for People with Disabilities. Addressing the players, he said: “For me, as a medical doctor and as a Minister of Sports, it is very important that we are starting with the Paralympic chess. You, representing 36 countries, 41 teams and around 200 chess players, are showing to the entire world the power, the passion, and will. I am very, very thankful to all of you that you trust in us and came here, and I wish all success to all of you.” His words captured one of the central messages of the evening: while chess dissolves boundaries across the board, it is the players themselves who demonstrate the power and determination behind every move. “A celebration of determination” Dana Reizniece, Deputy Chair of the FIDE Management Board, placed the opening in a broader historical context, connecting Samarkand’s ancient chess heritage with the rapid development of chess in modern Uzbekistan. She recalled chess pieces carved from ivory and discovered by archaeologists in the region, dating back more than a thousand years – a symbolic link between the game’s deep roots here and the chess events Samarkand is welcoming today. “More than 1,000 years ago, some people here were sitting and carved some chess pieces out of ivory, and seven of those were found by archaeologists. And this is, I guess, the seed that was embedded back there, taken by smart people, now nurtured by smart and capable governments, and creating the future of chess here in Samarkand and in Uzbekistan.” Reizniece noted the particular significance of Uzbekistan opening its doors to the participants of the Olympiad for People with Disabilities, the main Chess Olympiad and the FIDE Congress during the same major gathering. For her, however, the occasion represented something beyond chess itself: “I would say even more: a celebration of determination. Sometimes people are mistaken when they think what determination is about. They think it’s about being strong all the time, perfect, and never making mistakes. For me, it’s something more. I think it’s the ability to make the next move, to get up and flourish at the very difficult and the most difficult times again and again and again.” She drew a parallel between that determination and the nature of chess itself. “Chess is a very honest game. It doesn’t suggest that it’s going to be easy. It gives you the position as it is, and you have to make the next move.” She concluded with FIDE’s motto, Gens una sumus – “We are one family”, expressing the hope that this spirit would define the coming weeks in Samarkand. Poland draws White The sporting element of the evening came with the drawing of lots for the colors, conducted by Chief Arbiter Nebojsa Baralic. Akaki Iashvili, FIDE Special Tasks Director and FIDE Technical Delegate of the Olympiad for People with Disabilities, and Komil Sindarov, Vice President of the Uzbekistan Chess Federation, took part in the draw for top-seeded Poland. The result gave Poland White on the first board in Round 1. The first moves await With the official opening complete and the colors decided, attention now turns to the chessboards. The 3rd FIDE Chess Olympiad for People with Disabilities will be played as a seven-round Swiss team competition. The teams are composed of players with hearing impairments, physical disabilities and visual impairments, with at least one player of each gender required in the lineup for every round. Round 1 begins on September 11 at 15:00 local time. The competition continues with one round per day, with the seventh and final round scheduled for 11:00 on September 17. Five days after the first moves of the Olympiad for People with Disabilities, the 46th FIDE Chess Olympiad will begin on September 16, bringing the two Olympiads together in Samarkand. For the coming days, the chessboards will become a shared space where differences fade and the next move is what matters. Chess dissolves boundaries – and the players gathered in Samarkand are ready to show the power, passion and will to move beyond them. You can find pairings of the Round 1 on Chess-results. Follow the games live. Written by Angelika Valkova Photos: Mark Livshitz FIDE Chess Olympiad for People with Disabilities official website: https://dis-olympiad2026.fide.com/

title: Salesforce’s Agentforce 360 powers the future of chess with FIDE
summary: Salesforce becomes the Title Sponsor and Technological partner of FIDE. Partnership brings the Agentforce 360 portfolio, including Slack, to the world’s largest chess events and forums, powering real-time player rankings and AI-driven fan experiences for over 800 million global fans. SAN FRANCISCO and LAUSANNE – September 10, 2026 – Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the #1 AI CRM, today announced a landmark multi-year partnership with the International Chess Federation (FIDE), becoming the Title Sponsor of the FIDE World Championship Matches 2026-28 and the official AI partner of the FIDE World Chess Championship and FIDE Rankings. The collaboration will utilize the full power of Agentforce 360 – the complete portfolio of Salesforce AI solutions that power the Agentic Enterprise – to unify every layer of its operations, player rankings, and fan connections onto a single platform. This includes leveraging Slack to further connect FIDE’s global teams and streamline workflows. A Partnership Built for the Championship The partnership between FIDE and Salesforce covers the 2026 and 2028 World Championship Matches, the 2027 Women’s Match, and the world rankings. The official world championship matches and rankings will be presented as the Salesforce FIDE World Chess Championships and Salesforce FIDE Rankings. A new standard for chess: intelligence meets innovation FIDE has been the governing body of chess since 1924, today overseeing 204 national member federations, 1.5 million rated players, and tens of thousands of rated events per year across 195 countries. With Agentforce 360, FIDE will run its entire operation on a single, intelligent platform, unlocking new ways to connect with players, federations, and fans around the world. Fans will experience this transformation first-hand through the Chess Concierge Agent, powered by Agentforce 360, that answers questions on ratings, rules, and live tournament status for 1.2 million monthly visitors in any language. Internally, Agentforce 360 will help FIDE more efficiently run its operations. This includes powering Move of the Day: a workflow that analyzes moves from elite competition and surfaces them to the FIDE expert panel via Slack for final selection. Slack will also connect FIDE’s federations and commissions worldwide, giving officers behind-the-scenes visibility into ratings and operations. Core to FIDE’s authority is its rating system, the universally recognized measure of every chess player’s skill that is used to track standings, history, and predictive analysis. FIDE’s ELO Player Rating Agent will offer a conversational lookup of any FIDE player, including historic trends, current standings, insights into results, and predictions. It also automates the rating data pipelines across 204 federations – replacing manual batch processes with near real-time ratings. Underpinning this is Data 360, which will unify FIDE’s player database of active online chess players and 60,000+ annual event streams to offer consolidated real-time fan and player profiles. Emil Sutovsky, CEO of FIDE, said: “This is truly a landmark agreement. This partnership equips FIDE with enterprise-grade CRM and fan engagement tools from the world’s leading company to transform how we manage relationships with federations, players and audiences. Title sponsorship of the 2026 and 2028 Matches, along with the Women’s Match in 2027, demonstrates the partnership and commitment between FIDE and Salesforce.” Viswanathan Anand, FIDE Interim President, said: “This agreement places chess at the heart of technological innovation. Salesforce’s title sponsorship of the open and women’s cycles, plus our ranking system, shows genuine commitment. This will inspire a new generation and give our premier events the stage they deserve.” “Chess is one of the world’s most beloved games, cherished by hundreds of millions of people across every culture and corner of the globe,” said Patrick Stokes, President, Applications and Marketing, Salesforce. “We’re truly honored to partner with FIDE and bring the power of the Agentic Enterprise to a sport with such rich history and passionate fans. From the Salesforce FIDE World Chess Championships to the Salesforce FIDE Rankings, we want to help FIDE connect with its players and audiences in ways that feel personal, seamless, and worthy of the game they love.” About Salesforce Salesforce helps organizations of any size become Agentic Enterprises — integrating humans, agents, apps, and data on a trusted, unified platform to unlock unprecedented growth and innovation. Visit www.salesforce.com for more information. Media Contacts: Salesforce: pr@salesforce.com
